page: The Amazon Web Services r8gb.medium is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors operating at 2.8 GHz. Delivered via the AWS Nitro System hypervisor, this instance provision features a single dedicated physical core and single vCPU paired with 8.0 GB of system memory, matching an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Hardware acceleration flags include support for hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions, and provides a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps without complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark measurements reflect the single-core architecture of the AWS Neoverse-V2 core. In single-threaded processing, the instance achieves competitive results, including an average rating on Geekbench single-core at 1747.0 and stress-ng single-core at 1694.8, alongside strong performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 14.2 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core metrics—such as stress-ng multi-core (1694.8) and Geekbench multi-core (1745.0)—rank in the bottom tier relative to broader multi-core cloud instances due to the single-vCPU ceiling. Memory bandwidth benchmarks demonstrate 30.38 GB/sec read and 11.75 GB/sec write throughput on large uncached blocks.

With its 8 GB RAM allotment on a single dedicated core, the r8gb.medium provides cost-effective resource density for small memory-bound workloads that do not demand parallel computing pipelines. Primary trade-offs include the total absence of integrated NVMe storage, modest baseline network bandwidth, and strictly serialized execution bounds. It serves well for lightweight in-memory caching instances, small relational databases, microservices with high working-set footprints, and background utility tasks optimized for ARM64 architectures.
description: The Amazon Web Services r8gb.medium is an entry-tier memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an arm64 AWS Neoverse-V2 processor at 2.8 GHz. The server configuration features 1 dedicated vCPU, 8.0 GB of memory, and baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. It includes no bundled local storage and no dedicated GPUs. In benchmark assessments, the Neoverse-V2 core yields average single-core computing performance in Geekbench and stress-ng, along with strong single-threaded bzip3 decompression, while overall multi-core and memory write throughput remain limited by the single-core hardware ceiling. The 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio offers an efficient resource footprint for memory-centric, low-concurrency operations. The r8gb.medium is suitable for small in-memory caches, lightweight database services, ARM64 development environments, and applications requiring generous memory capacity without high parallel processing demands.
